unwalkedPanels.why: The home screen, and it is COVERED SOMEWHERE ELSE rather than uncovered: round-11.1/v1 "Constellation" is a WebGL canvas composition, so a computed-style walk can read nothing painted on it. tests/home.js measures it FROM THE PIXELS instead — 16 elements, worst 4.23:1, on the rendered frame — which check 14 already names. Two DOM checkers over one canvas would be one checker rotting.

The rail's scrim on a narrow window — a translucent sheet with no text in it and no boundary of its own, so it is neither a text node nor a non-text INDICATOR under check 3's definition. What matters about a scrim is what can still be read THROUGH it, and check 8 measures exactly that on every run: a 12% sheet takes 4.54:1 down to 4.25:1 and the 4.25 is what gets reported, not the stylesheet's 4.54.

The worker inspector's scrim, on the same footing as the rail's. The inspector ITSELF is walked (surface `inspector`, 146 nodes measured) — it is only the sheet beside it that carries nothing to measure.

floorReference.//: All surface counts come from the same 35-surface WebKit run. Newly shipped shared markup increased the shell from 462 to 466 considered nodes without changing its 92 measured nodes. Rebase all floors together to retain each surface contribution over that shell. The existing three-node tolerance and shrink compensation remain unchanged.
floorReference.measuredOn: 2026-09-17 macOS WebKit: all 34 surfaces in one run, after adding three speech-model walks (voice-model-offer / -progress / -failed). ONLY `considered` was rebased, and by exactly +10 on every surface: the four speech-model rows are markup inside #voice-panel and are therefore part of the shared shell (448 -> 458), while its 92 MEASURED nodes did not move, because those rows stay hidden until a machine with no speech model opens the panel. No `checked` floor was touched except the three new surfaces (98 each, which bites against the shell's 92 at tolerance 3). `saved-work` measures 118 checked against its committed 71 - pre-existing slack, unrelated to this work, deliberately NOT tightened on a branch that did not measure its variability. AMENDED SAME DAY, LATER, for audit D7's `.chrome-select` fix: the two selects named unstyled in the nightly audit each gained a custom chevron `<span>`, adding one hidden text node per theme to the shared shell (458 -> 462, `checked` unchanged). THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS AMENDMENT ASSERTED GROWTH NEVER NEEDS A REBASE, AND CHECK 9z DISAGREED ON THE SPOT: four thin surfaces (`permission`, `memory-setup`, `memory-no-compiler`, `updates-waiting`) had a considered-margin over the shell of exactly 4-6 nodes, and the shell's own +4 ate enough of that margin to put all four inside the three-node tolerance, so the bare shell would have cleared their floors — the precise failure 9z exists to catch. `>=` being monotone in the SURFACE's own considered count says nothing about its MARGIN over a shell that grew under it. So every existing floor's `considered` was rebased by the same +4, exactly as the four-days-of-precedent comment above this one already prescribes for shared-markup growth; every `checked` floor is untouched. Only the new `setup-account-connect` surface (the first driver to reach `#provider-account-select` visible) needed a floor of its own — checked 16 / considered 464 — declared in `cannotBite` because its own margin over the rebased shell (462) is inside tolerance. AMENDED AGAIN, on the branch that merged D7, for audit D5's first-run deferral: the company question gained a Not now and the line saying what deferring costs (#entity-picker-later, #entity-picker-defer-note), which is two more text nodes shipped in index.html and therefore two more on EVERY surface's considered count (462 -> 466). Check 9z named the same four thin surfaces it named for D7 — `permission`, `memory-setup`, `memory-no-compiler`, `updates-waiting` — for the same reason, which is the second independent confirmation that shared-markup growth always needs the rebase the note above prescribes. Measured rather than assumed: the delta was computed across all 35 surfaces and came back as the single value 4. `checked` moved on exactly one surface, `company-picker` +4 — the surface those two controls are VISIBLE on — and that is recorded rather than tolerated. Every other `checked` floor is untouched; the slack on `saved-work` (118 against 71) and on the three `updates-*` surfaces (+2) is pre-existing, measured identically before and after this work, and deliberately not tightened by a branch that did not measure its variability.
floorReference.toleranceWhy: Three nodes, and the number is bounded from both sides rather than picked. BELOW: the thinnest panel in the set, `first-run-unusable`, contributes 4 measured and 4 considered nodes over the bare shell, so a tolerance of 3 still fails if that panel vanishes — which is the whole job. ABOVE: measured surface-over-shell deltas moved by at most 2 between the 2026-09-06 runner run and this local one, across four days of product change and a different machine, so 3 covers the observed spread with one to spare.

cannotBite.opening-screen: The opening screen measures 0 of 450 nodes while the shell measures 92 of 448. Its two extra considered nodes are within the three-node tolerance, so the count floor cannot prove arrival. The driver instead holds the curtain and asserts RichSplash.state() still reports a held curtain with no dismissal reason.
cannotBite.settings: The assertiveness popover unhides existing markup: both it and the shell consider 448 nodes. It measures 74 against the shell's 92 because the panel obscures the shell. The driver requires #assertiveness-popover:not([hidden]) and awaits its completed entry animation; an unopened panel fails that wait.
cannotBite.settings-tooltip: The tooltip is stylesheet-generated content, not a DOM text node. Its node counts equal the shell's 92 of 448. The driver requires an opaque ::after pseudo-element, and check 11b separately requires the authored Settings string to be measured.
cannotBite.setup-account-connect: The account-type label and select are markup already in index.html's #setup-sheet, hidden until renderProviderAuth reaches a connectable state; the surface considers 464 nodes against the shell's 462 (post audit-D7 chevron spans), two apart and inside the three-node tolerance, so the count floor alone cannot prove arrival. The driver requires #provider-account-kind:not([hidden]), which only turns true once openAccountConnection -> renderProviderAuth sets canConnect for a provider state that is neither connected, unavailable nor connecting.
